statement: Under the two-item cyclic-Gray-code convention fixed in problem.md, for every connected unlabeled loopless simple graph G with 2 <= |V(G)| <= 6, AO(G) has a Hamiltonian cycle if and only if sigma(G)=0. The complete domain has 142 isomorphism classes by orders 2,3,4,5,6 in counts 1,2,6,21,112. Exactly 125 classes are Hamiltonian, in counts 1,2,5,18,99 by order; they are exactly the sigma-zero entries of evidence/atlas-through-6.json and each has the explicit cycle in evidence/hamilton-cycles.json. The other 17 classes are non-Hamiltonian by parity imbalance, with canonical graph6 identifiers C], DFw, DLs, D]{, E?~o, E@vg, E@vo, EBj?, EBjW, EBjg, EBz_, EBzw, EB~o, EJeg, EJnW, ELvg, E]~o. Consequently sigma(G)=0 is sufficient throughout the frozen domain and there are no counterexamples, minimum-order or otherwise, in it.
contribution: This supplies a complete, replayable finite atlas for the frozen 142-class problem: exhaustive canonical representatives, all acyclic orientations and flip edges, independently verified Hamilton cycles for every positive case, and an exact parity obstruction for every negative case. The cited paper reports 22 selected named examples rather than this complete order-at-most-six atlas; no broader priority claim is made beyond the bounded comparison in problem.md.
